seo.metaTitle: PNG Dithering Tool - Floyd-Steinberg and Bayer, Free
seo.metaDescription: Reduce a picture to 2 to 16 colors without the flat banding, using Floyd-Steinberg error diffusion or an ordered Bayer 4x4 pattern. Free, no upload, runs locally.
seo.longDescription: Dithering is how a picture is reduced to very few colors without the harsh flat patches that usually come with it. The tool builds a small palette from the image, then either diffuses the rounding error into neighbouring pixels with Floyd-Steinberg or adds an ordered Bayer 4x4 offset before choosing the nearest palette color. The result uses only a handful of colors yet keeps the gradients readable. It runs in your browser on PNG, JPG, WebP and BMP files, nothing is uploaded, and the alpha channel is untouched.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Set Color count between 2 and 16; 4 is a good starting point for a picture that should still read as a picture.
Choose Pattern: Floyd-Steinberg for a photographic look, Bayer 4x4 for a regular visible grid.
Download the result from the Download button.

faq.a: Floyd-Steinberg scatters the error as fine random-looking speckle and suits photos and gradients. Bayer 4x4 adds the same offset per position in a repeating four by four tile, so the texture is an even ordered pattern that fits retro and pixel-art looks.

faq.q: Why does my image look noisy?
faq.a: That noise is the point: the error each pixel leaves behind is carried into its neighbours, which is how four colors can suggest a smooth sky. At 2 or 3 colors the speckle becomes obvious, so raise the Color count or switch to Bayer.
No. The pixels are rewritten in place - the result is the same size as the source, with the same alpha channel, just painted with palette colors.

faq.q: Can I use my own colors?
faq.a: Not on this page - the palette is built from the image by the same median-cut engine the quantize tool uses. If you need specific colors, name them in the custom palette tool first.
